lines: # Conditional reference laws for short inscriptions: copies, selection and fitting feasibility

Private working manuscript, 2 October 2026. Main comparisons, finite calculations and shared-quality follow-ups have completed independent audits. Authorship, affiliations and venue remain to be supplied. Computational analysis and writing used AI assistance. Code snapshots, finite tables, proposals, results and audits are retained in the project repository.
## Abstract

Permutation references for short inscriptions depend on the process that produced and selected the records. We examine those dependencies through finite enumeration and known simulated populations. Across 1,000 literal-copy populations, individual-record shuffling rejects 15.9% at nominal 5%, while object shuffling rejects 5.4%; the paired excess is 10.5 percentage points, with a 95% interval of 8.5–12.6. With two imperfect faces per object, rates are 11.0% and 5.0%, excess 6.0 points, interval 4.3–7.7. Six balanced binary records admit 8,000 column tables, including 2,880 distinct-string tables. Rejection sampling is uniform on that subset. Deduplicating seven independent draws into six retained strings instead gives unequal subset masses: a uniform-unique reference rejects 5.1537% at its 5% cutoff, while a matched selected-law reference gives 4.9407%. A same-margin witness exposes an undefined fit, and explicit score extension and feasibility conditioning give different rejection fractions among usable observations. With quality shared across slots, the preserved prediction statistic rejects 4% versus 3% under broad and quality-conditioned vector references on 300 populations. A post-outcome observed-agreement statistic, fixed before 1,000 fresh populations, gives 94.2% versus 1.0%; exact conditional tails give 95.0% versus .8%. The collection specifies sampling law, fitting domain and statistic sensitivity together.
## 1. The record process belongs in the reference question

A catalogue can contain independent objects, several impressions from one stamp, two faces of one object, or several descriptions of the same inscription. A reference that moves each row independently gives those cases the same freedom. A reference that keeps object observations together preserves a different set of possible tables. The question is whether those tables follow the law claimed for the observed population.

The project previously measured held-out local predictive gain in selected Indus transcriptions. Its main reference shuffles exact length/slot columns within site/type strata and rebuilds physical/text groups, folds and model selection for every proposal. A unique-string sensitivity rejects proposals that introduce a repeated whole string. [Original methods](../001-artifact-aware-prediction/methods.md). The present study examines the conditional sampling laws underlying that procedure. Its data are finite combinatorial tables and generated populations with specified dependence. They permit exact probabilities and independent replay.

The statistical principles have established precedents. Phipson and Smyth describe finite random-reference p-values, including the observed score in the rank calculation. Hemerik and Goeman develop exact random-permutation testing. Winkler and colleagues give block permutation methods for related observations. Hurlbert's experimental-design treatment explains how replicated observations depend on the experimental unit. Our contribution is the collection of explicit table laws, measured calibration outcomes and preserved domain failures for this short-record fitting procedure. [Primary rank source](https://gksmyth.github.io/pubs/PermPValuesPreprint.pdf), [exact testing](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11749-017-0571-1), [block permutation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4644991/), [experimental units](https://doi.org/10.2307/1942661).
## 2. Statistic, sampling and checks
### 2.1 The preserved fitting statistic

The statistic is held-out dependent-minus-independent log score, measured in bits per noninitial sign. Physical aliases and identical whole strings define edges in a transitive component graph. Five outer folds keep components intact. Three inner folds select an independent unigram, length/slot or length/slot/metadata model and the local-dependency strength. The smoothing grid is 5, 20, 100, 500 and 2,000. Every observed and reference corpus repeats grouping, fold allocation, training-only selection and scoring from unchanged method snapshots. [Main protocol](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/MAIN_PROTOCOL.md), [snapshot hashes](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/sources/).

For 99 independently drawn reference scores, the one-sided Monte Carlo p-value is `(1 + exceedances)/100`, with equality included in the exceedance count. Exact finite calculations instead sum the full declared tail probability. Rejection fractions are reported at 1%, 5% and 10%. Monte Carlo rate intervals describe the generated trial collection. The conditional rank argument assumes that the observed and reference tables follow the same conditional law and that the fitting statistic is defined on its support.

Physical sampling blocks and held-out components serve different purposes. A physical block identifies observations tied by the generating process. A component identifies records excluded together from fitting. Rebuilding the latter on a shuffled table prevents a fitting leak; it does not alter that table's sampling probability. Both structures are saved and audited.
### 2.2 Conditional column spaces

Within a fixed length/slot/metadata cell, independent categorical draws give a table probability determined by the sign counts. Conditioning on those counts makes every labeled arrangement equiprobable. If a cell has `n` entries and category counts `m(v)`, it has `n!/∏m(v)!` distinct arrangements. Every arrangement has `∏m(v)!` generating labeled permutations. Repeated values therefore have equal multiplicity across arrangements.

Whole-string uniqueness restricts the complete table space. Uniform column proposals accepted only when all row strings differ remain uniform on that subset. This follows by conditioning a uniform proposal on its acceptance event. The waiting time changes computational cost; the accepted table law follows the restriction. We verify those probabilities by full enumeration and independent sampler counts. [Mathematical derivation](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/MATHEMATICS.md).
### 2.3 Physical observations and imperfect faces

Literal copies share a latent object's signs. Their matched reference permutes slot columns among objects within strata, then expands each object to its declared records. Equal copy counts preserve latent and expanded margins together. Unequal counts require weighted constraints or a reference conditioned on additional copy classes.

The imperfect-face experiment has twenty objects, two faces per object, three slots and eight categories. An observed face retains the latent sign with probability .9; otherwise it selects uniformly among the other seven signs. Face errors are independent conditional on that sign. The ordered vector of both face signs has probability `r(a,b)=Σ p(x)K(a|x)K(b|x)`. Conditioning on vector counts in a cell makes its labeled vector arrangements uniform. Permuting whole vectors preserves that joint margin and each face's scalar margin. [Observation law](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/noisy-faces/METHODS.md).

This experiment compares vector shuffling with individual-record column shuffling on the same 1,000 observed populations. Each case has 99 reference corpora per method. The original score and nested procedure are unchanged. Distinct seed namespaces prevent overlap between reference streams. An audit reconstructs all observations and proposals, joint margins, aliases, graph components, fold loads, p-values and aggregates, then repeats fifteen complete fits.
## 3. Finite spaces expose the sampling distinctions
### 3.1 Uniqueness conditioning

Six labeled binary records with three ones in each of three columns have `20³=8,000` complete tables. There are eight possible whole strings. Selecting six distinct strings with balanced columns requires omitting one complementary pair. Four possible omitted pairs and `6!` label arrangements give 2,880 unique tables. The exact rejection-sampler acceptance probability is .36, and every accepted table has probability `1/2,880`.

The preserved nested statistic was fitted on all 2,880 unique tables. Its inclusive tails reject exactly 5% at the 5% cutoff. Independent enumeration checks table identity, permutation multiplicity, acceptance and every saved tail. The ordinary tiny space includes component counts too small for the original five-fold fit; those cases motivated the separately specified domain experiment below. [Exact endpoint](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/exact/results.json), [independent audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/verification_exact.json).
### 3.2 Deduplication as an observed selection process

Drawing seven raw independent strings and retaining each distinct string once supplies a different law. Let the three binary slot probabilities be .2, .3 and .4. Condition on six retained strings with three ones in each retained column, then assign their row labels uniformly. The four support masses are 21.3333%, 24.6667%, 26.6667% and 27.3333%, ordered by omitted pairs `000/111`, `001/110`, `010/101` and `011/100`. A population directly conditioned on six unique strings gives 25% to each.

For support `S`, the seven-draw probability is proportional to `∏q(x) Σq(x)` over its retained strings. The fixed retained margins fix the product, while the sum varies. Each support spreads its mass over 720 row arrangements. Reweighting the existing nested scores gives a 5.1537% rejection fraction when the uniform-unique reference is retained. Matching the reference to the selected law gives 4.9407%. The largest excess over a nominal attainable cutoff is .6046 percentage points in this finite process. [Exact probabilities and tails](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/dedup-selection/results.json).

An independent recurrence propagates probabilities over the set of strings seen after each raw draw. It verifies the four support masses without using the occupancy formula and checks all 11,520 stored tail values. This example identifies the selection assumption required to interpret a uniqueness-conditioned reference beyond its selected population.
### 3.3 Copies and weighted margins

Four binary latent objects with balanced columns have 216 tables. Two copies per object expand them into eight records. Ordinary record columns admit 343,000 balanced tables, of which 216 preserve the declared copy pairs. Their supported-space probability is about .000630 under that ordinary reference. The matched object law stays on the copy-supported space.

An integer adjacency statistic permits exact expanded-space tails as copy count grows. Three copies per object give a 25% false-rejection fraction under the ordinary reference at its 5% cutoff. The matched object reference rejects 2.78%. Its smallest tail occupies six of the 216 tables, so tied ranks make it conservative. A separate integer dynamic program verifies the ordinary distributions for one through five copies. [Exact copy experiment](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/copy-tail-counts/README.md).

With unequal multiplicities `[1,1,1,2,2,3]`, fixing three latent ones and five expanded ones leaves six compatible columns. Unrestricted object shuffling preserves the expanded margin in only six of its twenty possible columns. A continuation-count sampler chooses each next sign in proportion to its exact number of legal completions. Every final column has probability `1/6`; three slots give 216 equiprobable tables. Both direct and rejection samplers preserve the constraints in 100,000 draws each. The direct stream's Pearson statistic is 263.5194 on 215 degrees of freedom, with p=.01336 at its declared seed. Exact branch probabilities and an independent replay remain available beside that uneven sample count. [Weighted conditional space](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/unequal-copy-counts/README.md).
## 4. Calibration in the full fitting procedure
### 4.1 Independent records, selected unique records and literal copies

The original main study generates 1,000 populations for each of three laws: independent slot draws, those draws conditioned on distinct whole strings, and two identical records per latent object. Each population has forty three-slot records and eight categories in two equal site/type strata. Slot probabilities are `[.20,.16,.14,.12,.11,.10,.09,.08]`, cyclically shifted right by `site index + 2 × slot index`. Unique populations reject and redraw the complete forty-record proposal when any whole string repeats. Copied populations have twenty latent objects, ten per stratum, each expanded into two identical records. Each population receives 99 reference draws; copied populations receive both record-column and object-column references. This gives 3,000 observed fits and 396,000 reference fits. All methods repeat the complete nested statistic.
| Population and reference | Rejection at 1% | At 5% | At 10% |
| Independent records, record columns | 1.1% | 5.0% | 9.9% |
| Unique records, uniqueness-conditioned columns | 1.1% | 5.9% | 10.6% |
| Literal copies, object columns | 1.1% | 5.4% | 10.3% |
| Literal copies, record columns | 4.8% | 15.9% | 27.0% |

At 5%, the marginal Wilson intervals for copied populations are 4.162–6.979% with object references and 13.765–18.296% with record references. Their paired excess is 10.5 percentage points, with a 20,000-draw interval of 8.5–12.6 points. The saved seed schedule links object-reference trial `i` to record-reference trial `i+500` in 500 pairs. Each method's marginal trials have distinct streams; the paired calculation resamples the 500 linked clusters to preserve the covariance between methods. The independent audit reconstructs all 928,424 proposals, all 396,000 accepted graph/fold allocations and every p-value, and repeats 33 complete fits. [Frozen endpoint](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/main/results.json), [full audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/verification_main.json), [paired seed audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/paired_seed_audit.json).
### 4.2 Imperfect faces

At nominal 1%, 5% and 10% thresholds, the matched face-vector reference rejects 0.5%, 5.0% and 10.4% of the 1,000 simulated populations. The individual-record reference rejects 2.5%, 11.0% and 19.6%. At 5%, the Wilson intervals are 3.813–6.531% and 9.208–13.091%, respectively. The paired difference is 6.0 percentage points, with a 20,000-draw bootstrap interval of 4.3–7.7 points. There are 41 joint rejections, 69 record-only, nine vector-only and 881 joint nonrejections. [Frozen main result](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/noisy-faces/main/results.json), [full audit and paired calculations](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/noisy-faces/verification_main.json).

All 99,000 individual-record references change the joint vector margins. The 99,000 matched references preserve them. Recomputed components range from fifteen to twenty in observed tables, nine to twenty in record references, and thirteen to twenty in vector references. Thus both methods account for their proposed tables during fitting, while their proposal laws still differ.

Across 60,000 observed object slots, 48,821 pairs agree. The observation kernel predicts agreement probability `142/175`, and whole-string agreement probability `(142/175)³`. Among 20,000 objects, 10,817 observed strings are equal. The audit also records 11,868 replacements in 120,000 face slots. Those checks locate the simulation's supplied error law; they are not fitted archaeological error rates.
## 5. Fitting feasibility and observed abstention

The original fitting algorithm requires enough groups for nonempty outer folds and inner selection. A twenty-object witness connects consecutive objects through shared complete strings. Transitive physical/text closure makes one component, and the preserved fit raises `ZeroDivisionError`. A within-stratum ordered-vector shuffle creates twenty components and a finite score with the same vector margins. Both tables have positive probability under the declared imperfect-face generator. [Witness, failure and shuffled table](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/domain-support/main-v2/results.json).

The conditional sampler's table law is well defined in that witness, while the original statistic is only partially defined. A subsequent frozen protocol compares two explicit responses on all 8,000 binary tables. The first assigns zero gain to reference tables with fewer than five components and abstains when the observed table is unusable. The second conditions the reference on the usable subset. Of all tables, 5,760 are usable and 2,240 trigger abstention.

| Nominal cutoff | Extended law over all observations | Extended law among usable observations | Feasibility-conditioned reference among usable observations | Conditioned reference over all observations, including abstention |

At 5%, 400 extended-law rejections occupy 5% of all tables and 6.9444% of usable tables. A feasibility-conditioned reference changes the denominator and rejects 276 of 5,760 usable tables. Independent graph traversal checks all component counts, and score-frequency counting checks all full and conditional tails. The experiment reuses 2,880 frozen unique scores and adds the 2,880 five-component fits. [Guard protocol](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/domain-support/GUARD_PROTOCOL.md), [exact result](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/domain-support/guard-exact/results.json), [verification](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/domain-support/verification.json).

The finite example distinguishes calibration over a declared population from calibration after reporting only usable observations. A future reference implementation needs its score extension, abstention policy or selection law specified before fitting.

A separate constructive bound establishes fitting feasibility for some original main reference laws. If each physical block contains one complete string and blocks have no other physical links, joining equal strings yields one component per distinct string. The number of codes used in any fixed slot bounds that component count below. Singleton-record column references preserve this premise; matched literal-copy references preserve it at the object level. The original independent and unique margins supply a bound of eight components, and copied-object margins supply six to eight. Five positive-weight components suffice for the actual greedy outer and inner allocations to remain nonempty. An audit checks all 3,000 margins, all 396,000 saved reference groupings and 29,169 allocation cases. Record-column references on copies violate the one-string-per-block premise in all 99,000 sampled tables, so the bound applies to their object comparator only. The same premise fails in the imperfect-face domain witness. [Bound protocol](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/domain-support/SUPPORT_PROTOCOL.md), [completed support audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/domain-support/support-bound/results.json).
## 6. Estimating the supplied observation channel

A bounded follow-up fits the known symmetric kernel to the 1,000 frozen imperfect-face populations. Agreement identifies the shared replacement rate on its positive-association branch. If `H` is observed agreement, the direct estimate is `(7/8)[1−sqrt((8H−1)/7)]`, with the declared endpoint handling. A penalized ordered-pair likelihood jointly estimates the rate and each cell's latent distribution. It uses fixed Dirichlet(1.5) cell penalties, a Beta(1.5,1.5) rate penalty and three starts. A matched shrinkage baseline was added before fitting. [Protocol and comparison amendment](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/noisy-channel/PROTOCOL.md), [method and results](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/noisy-channel/README.md).

The true rate is .1. Agreement and joint mean estimates are .099261 and .101605, with mean absolute errors .023162 and .022195. Direct known-rate frequency inversion yields 10,335 negative components across 5,466 of 6,000 ten-object cells. Exact absence probabilities predict 10,331.87 negatives across these 1,000 populations. A constrained joint estimate has mean frequency total variation .245280, compared with .334097 for projected inversion using the agreement-estimated rate and .227690 for matched shrinkage. Pooling each of the six site/slot cells across the 1,000 populations uses sixty thousand observed pairs in total. Mean cell total variation is then .012236 for joint correction and .020967 for raw marginals. Small-cell estimation and pooled correction therefore have different measured outcomes.

An independent audit reconstructs every pair table, four thousand objectives and traces, six thousand projection checks, eight fits and the 20,000 bootstrap draws. Exact agreement-count and category-set recurrences supply separate sampling checks. Uniform latent frequencies also give an explicit unequal-observer rate ambiguity; nonuniform marginals identify the rate ratio under the declared kernel. [Recovery audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/noisy-channel/main/verification.json), [identification calculation](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/noisy-channel/IDENTIFICATION.md). A kernel with correlated faces or shared object quality needs its own observation model.
### 6.1 Quality shared across slots

A fresh follow-up assigns each object a fixed observed low-error or high-error class, with replacement rates .025 and .60. Each site has five objects of each class. Latent slots have the same distribution in both classes and remain independent. Both references move complete ordered face vectors; one moves them within broad site/type strata, and the other also preserves quality-specific vector counts. The fitting statistic continues to use its original site/type stratum and ignores quality. A zero-gain extension below five components and observed abstention were declared before generation.

At nominal 5%, broad references reject twelve of 300 populations, or 4.0%, and quality-conditioned references reject nine, or 3.0%. The paired difference is one percentage point, interval −1 to 3. Their marginal Wilson intervals are 2.303–6.860% and 1.586–5.602%. No observed or reference table used the guard. All 29,700 broad proposals change the quality-specific vector margins, while all 29,700 conditioned proposals preserve them. The independent audit reconstructs every population and all 59,400 references, then replays sixteen fits. [Frozen quality comparison](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/shared-quality/main/results.json), [audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/shared-quality/verification_main.json).

The exact small space has six columns with unequal probabilities given broad counts. Additional quality-specific counts leave four uniform columns and sixty-four uniform three-slot tables. An independent replay checks all 20,000 sampler draws. The maximum adjacent single-face event covariance is .0006072704 under the supplied mixture; the ordered-vector maximum is .0057955982. The reference law and the preserved score's sensitivity therefore have separate measured evidence: exact unequal table weights coexist with a small paired calibration difference in this main. [Exact laws](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/shared-quality/exact/results.json), [exact moments](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/shared-quality/analytic-moments/results.json).
### 6.2 A statistic directed at shared quality

The small nested-score difference motivated a separately specified diagnostic on 1,000 fresh populations. Let `A(o,i)` indicate agreement between object `o`'s two observed faces at slot `i`. The integer statistic `S=Σ_o[A(o,0)A(o,1)+A(o,1)A(o,2)]` counts adjacent agreement events and ranges from zero to forty. It uses the observed signs and fixed object pairs. Quality labels enter the reference grouping only. The score, sample budget and exact-tail calculation were fixed before these populations were generated. This is a post-outcome sensitivity experiment following Section 6.1. [Diagnostic protocol](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/shared-quality/agreement-diagnostic/PROTOCOL.md).
| Nominal cutoff | Broad reference, 99 draws | Quality reference, 99 draws | Broad reference, exact tail | Quality reference, exact tail |

At 5%, the Monte Carlo paired difference is 93.2 percentage points, with a 20,000-draw population-bootstrap interval of 91.6–94.7. The supplied generator's expected score is 18.9712, while its average broad-reference conditional expectation is 13.5058. Their difference is 5.4654. The fresh run has mean observed score 18.855, broad conditional mean 13.4469 and quality conditional mean 18.8614. Broad column shuffling redistributes the high- and low-agreement vectors separately at each slot. Quality-conditioned shuffling retains their concentration within each object's fixed class. [Frozen diagnostic](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/shared-quality/agreement-diagnostic/main/results.json).

For a reference cell with `n` objects and agreement counts `a0,a1,a2`, the conditional score mean is `(a0*a1+a1*a2)/n`. A row-state dynamic program gives exact integer multiplicities for all count triples at cell sizes five and ten. A second calculation conditions on the middle column and convolves two hypergeometric overlap distributions. It independently verifies all 1,547 cell distributions. Convolving the appropriate cell distributions supplies the 2,000 exact population tails. The audit also reconstructs all 1,000 populations, 198,000 reference tables, 199,000 scores and every reported tail and interval. [Independent audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/null-calibration/shared-quality/agreement-diagnostic/verification.json).

Inclusive integer ties and constant-score configurations make the quality-conditioned tails conservative. The original nested statistic's 4% versus 3% result remains alongside this agreement statistic's 94.2% versus 1.0%. The two experiments show how strongly a reported calibration rate can depend on the statistic's sensitivity to the supplied recording mechanism.
## 7. Application and availability

An archaeological application needs an observation model for which records belong to one artifact, which objects are literal copies, how uncertain faces were encoded, and how catalogue selection or deduplication changed the population. These inputs determine the conditional table law. A new archive with unequal record multiplicities can use the weighted-count calculation once those physical relations are established. A candidate-error model can preserve ordered alternative vectors when its observation premises are stated.

The results here support selecting and testing those premises with explicit counterexamples. The original Indus analyses remain conditional on their selected transcription population. Their predictive gains and p-values have separate evidence files; the present synthetic studies supply measured behavior under known laws and identify changes needed for broader sampling claims.

All finite tables, authored code, method snapshots, generated results, protocols and retrospectives are preserved privately. The [methods and evidence map](methods.md) gives reproduction paths and exact claim files. Raw archaeological corpora and unresolved-rights witnesses remain local under their source manifests. Frozen endpoints preserve failed fits and earlier designs beside their documented refinements.

lines: # Physical observations in numerical decoding: constraints, acquisition and a khipu control

Private working manuscript, 2 October 2026. Authorship, affiliations and venue are pending. Computational analysis and writing used AI assistance. The linked protocols, outputs and source records form the review package.
## Abstract

A proposed numerical reading must connect marks to independently observed quantities or relations. We study how physical membership, positional addresses and counts constrain unknown positive symbol values. In a six-label simulation, twelve complete whole–part observations identified relative values in all 24 generated collections; one count fixed scale. A subsequent acquisition experiment recovered absolute values in 23 of 24 complete-data worlds using an information/rank policy, compared with 15 under random selection. Inaccurate exact counts could identify a wrong scale that passed every withheld whole–part relation. A known-system control reproduced 16 of 20 columns in the published Puruchuco khipu account alignment. Generated decimal accounts identified the remaining positional values in 299 of 300 complete worlds after a counted unit fixed the first value. With unreliable local membership, a separate complete-inventory constraint increased recovery from 133 to 190 of 200 four-swap worlds and reduced accepted errors from nine to one. Incorrect completeness produced fifteen accepted errors. One wrong decoder passed eight fresh relations of rank one but failed independent counts. We provide exact solution certificates, preserved failures and an observation table for applying these methods to unfamiliar numerical records.
## 1. The observation that makes a reading testable

Suppose an unfamiliar object carries a mark beside three smaller objects. A proposed reading may assign a quantity to the mark. If the smaller objects demonstrably belong to the marked parent, their measured quantities can constrain the proposal. Repeated whole–part relations constrain relative values, while an independent count can establish absolute scale. The task is to identify which observations provide those constraints and which alternatives remain compatible.

This question is relevant to Indus numerical proposals because short stroke groups, vessel marks and multi-face tablets invite arithmetic interpretations. The project's earlier audit of a published two-equation proposal found several positive integer solutions under its unrestricted premises. Additional chosen ranges selected one system. The source review also found that the proposed external bangle count lacked an authenticated inscription-specific join. [Exact audit](../../research/methods/NUMERICAL_CONSTRAINT_AUDIT.md), [source premises](../../research/literature/metrology/numerical_source_premises.json). That result motivates acquiring a relation whose origin and units can be checked separately from the proposed reading.

Known numerical systems provide controls. Urton's study of khipu archives documents duplicate accounts and identity labels. The Khipu Field Guide publishes an explicit Puruchuco account comparison, with its partitions, values and discrepancies. Those records allow us to test how representation affects an already specified relation. [Urton 2005 author manuscript](https://dash.harvard.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/7312037e-6b09-6bd4-e053-0100007fdf3b/content), [published field-guide calculation](https://khipufieldguide.com/notebook/appendix/notebooks/12%20-%20Replicating%20Purucucho.html).

We supply an additive quantity hypothesis and ask whether the available observations identify its positive values. The study combines generated controls, a published-source replication and a collection design. The generated answer keys establish numerical correctness; primary artifact sources supply acquisition targets.
## 2. Methods
### 2.1 Physical membership and scale

The first simulation generates 24 collections with six concealed positive values. Label frequencies are balanced across the text-only observation pool. A complete assembly contributes an equation: its parent's value equals the sum of the labelled child values. Twelve training assemblies and eight withheld assemblies are generated per collection. One independently counted object supplies an absolute measurement. The solver receives label identities, membership and the count, while the answer key remains in a separate saved input. [PHYS-01 protocol and current endpoint](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-information/README.md).

Let `v` contain the unknown positive values and let `A` record parent-minus-child coefficients. Complete relations give `A v = 0`. Five independent rows can identify one positive relative ray for six labels. A count intersects that ray at a scale. Incomplete groups contribute inequalities, `parent ≥ visible children`, when the missingness is declared. Exact fractions preserve ranks, solutions and counterexamples.

We distinguish unrestricted positive values from a finite diagnostic that supplies the six-value bag. That diagnostic has a stronger prior and can select a mapping before the unrestricted relations identify it. Controls scramble membership, treat incomplete groups as complete, or give labels an ownership purpose with independently assigned object quantities. A corrected endpoint repairs an ownership-count error found while preparing the separated input interface. The initial output and correction remain available.
### 2.2 Choosing observations

A fresh acquisition experiment gives each policy public action descriptors, costs and a budget of 24 units. The descriptors disclose completeness and a bounded child-count menu. An inspection reveals a whole–part relation; a count measures a named object. Unopened responses and hidden quantities remain outside the selector. The surviving positive set is represented by equalities, inequalities and measured intervals. Exact optimization certificates support classification and planning calculations. [PHYS-02 protocol and methods](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-acquisition/METHODS.md).

The original policies choose by information/rank, at random or by the cheapest available action. They run on 24 worlds for each of five conditions: complete groups, incomplete groups, valid count intervals, counts with insufficient reported uncertainty, and ownership labels. Success requires the correct absolute vector; relative identification and remaining scale intervals are recorded separately. Policies continue to the budget boundary, so the first identification cost differs from total expenditure.

A post-outcome refinement addresses interval measurements. The first information rule assigned no value to an interval when the existing range was narrower than the interval width. A shifted interval could still trim that range. A separately specified overlap rule uses `w/(w+2r)`, where `w` is current range width and `r` the measurement radius. It was tested on 24 fresh interval worlds with all four policies. Its assumptions and original failed rule remain in separate endpoints.
### 2.3 Puruchuco representation control

The Open Khipu Repository was pinned to commit `4039ca51f4de661d80d0160596309c983a62a9c7`. Six original Puruchuco accounts join to stable database identifiers. CM009 is a field-guide reconstruction from an earlier thesis and remains a separate witness. Every selected pendant attachment-position field and every selected knot-cluster total field is zero. The reference values therefore come from the guide's published calculation, with source coordinates and hashes. [KHI-01 source audit](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/SOURCE_AUDIT.md).

The fixed predictor adds UR068 pendant ranges 14–33, 34–53 and 54–73 by column, then compares the twenty results with UR067 pendants 13–32. Source review exposed the target values before the protocol was frozen. This part is a reference replication with a programmatically isolated predictor and evaluator. It keeps the published alignment and all four mismatches.

Controls preserve an ordered flat list with known width, reverse selected rows' column order, apply all 400 relative cyclic shifts, perform 10,000 within-row shuffles, or allocate the sixty-value bag into three equal rows 10,000 times. Whole-row permutations are an additive invariance check. Each control preserves the lower total, so column-wise error provides the useful distinction. [KHI-01 methods](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/METHODS.md).
### 2.4 Hidden positional values

A separate simulation generates 300 worlds for each of three account conditions. Each world has eight accounts with three leaf quantities. Complete-account parents store their sum; ownership parents have independent quantities. Quantities have three digit positions, whose true values are 1, 10 and 100. The solver receives positional digit counts, physical membership and a counted one-unit object. That object's feature vector `(1,0,0)` fixes the first positional value at one. Account relations constrain the two remaining values. The solver receives no known value bag.

For each account, the parent's feature vector minus the summed children's feature vectors supplies a linear equation. Exact row reduction and strict positivity classify each prefix as uniquely positive, ambiguous or infeasible. The evaluator checks unique decoders against all 32 generated quantities. Representations retain membership, reorder siblings, omit membership, collapse positions or scramble children across parents. Incomplete accounts lose one child's membership in four accounts; ownership records assign parent quantities independently. A protocol supplement specified prefix evaluation before execution. [KHI-01 simulation and verification](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/endpoints/main-v1/aggregate.json).
### 2.5 Uncertain membership and collective inventories

A fresh 300-seed experiment replaces all-equation fitting with maximum consensus among the eight local account relations. With the first positional value fixed, the positive domain has two free values. Exact intersections and line families retain every tied optimum. The primary support gate requires six of eight accounts; a secondary gate requires four. Conditions include two or four swapped assignments, missing associations and independent ownership values. Held-out account relations and independent counts evaluate each accepted decoder. The protocols and all earlier-prefix outcomes are saved. [KHI-03 methods](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/robust-decoder/METHODS.md).

KHI-04 then generates 200 fresh base seeds under seven observation conditions. All visible local account rows enter the support vote as equalities, including rows with missing associations. An independent inventory associates all eight parents with the pooled child collection. The proposed operation uses the same quantity type, units and event; parent marks describe contents pooled without loss or exchange. For a complete collection it gives a binding equality; a declared partial collection gives an inequality. Swapping local members preserves the complete collective equality. All parent and pooled-child marks are available before the first local prefix, with no assigned inventory-acquisition cost. The collective relation enters as a hard constraint and adds no local support vote. Two scale views are retained: normalized first value one represents a positive ray, while an independent unit-feature count fixes that world's absolute scale. The same 75% and 50% support gates are applied. [Collective protocol and observation availability](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/conservation-check/METHODS.md).
### 2.6 Select validation rows before opening targets

A post-outcome follow-up reuses KHI-04's sealed worlds and final candidate sets. Each world offers eight held-out account coefficient rows and three count-feature rows. The selector receives those rows, observation types, budget and any available unit-anchor coefficient row. Measured targets, decoder candidates, world condition and true values remain outside selection. Account-first, count-first and greedy coefficient-rank policies use budgets zero through three. Uniform-random subsets are enumerated exactly. Each check costs one abstract unit; acquisition effort and measurement uncertainty are absent. Validation intersects the original optimum points, rays and positive families with selected measured equations and retains the original support gate. [KHI-05 protocol and input separation](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/validation-design/METHODS.md).
## 3. Results
### 3.1 Relations determine ratios; counts determine scale

Twelve complete assemblies identify the correct positive relative vector in all 24 six-label collections. One count then identifies every absolute vector. At three assemblies, the finite value-bag diagnostic already selects one assignment in 12 collections, while no unrestricted positive relative vector is unique. At eight assemblies, the finite diagnostic is unique in all 24, while the unrestricted model identifies 23. [PHYS-01 corrected results](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-information/main-corrected-anchor/results.json).

With six incomplete groups entered as inequalities, 17 collections retain a unique relative ray. Seven admit a second positive integer assignment after the count. For collection 20261015, both `(6,8,1,2,4,3)` and `(12,8,2,4,8,2)` satisfy every acquired constraint and the measured value eight on label `g1`. Withheld complete assemblies reject the alternative. [Exact integer witnesses](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-information/integer-ambiguity-certificates.json).

Five short-prefix controls produce an incorrect positive relative ray: two scrambled collections and three incomplete collections treated as complete. Each fails at least one of the eight withheld relations; their failure counts are six, five, six, six and eight. A unique solution under an acquired subset can therefore be followed into a separate empirical check.
### 3.2 Observation choice changes recovery cost
| Condition | Information/rank: correct absolute vectors | Random | Cheapest |
| Complete groups and exact counts | 23/24 | 15/24 | 0/24 |
| Incomplete groups and exact counts | 22/24 | 17/24 | 1/24 |
| Valid count intervals | 1/24 | 1/24 | 0/24 |
| Counts with insufficient uncertainty | 0/24 | 0/24 | 0/24 |
| Ownership labels | 0/24 | 0/24 | 0/24 |

Information/rank identifies quantities earlier than random in all 15 common complete-data successes, saving a mean 6.47 cost units. Across 17 common incomplete-data successes, it saves 9.82 units on average; it is faster in 16 and slower in one. One complete world has no available count, so its identified ratios retain unfixed scale. Opening all available evidence after the frozen run distinguishes one irreducibly ambiguous incomplete world from another that needs acquisition beyond the original budget. [Main acquisition analysis](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-acquisition/main-analysis/analysis.json).

Valid intervals usually leave a scale interval. The refined overlap policy recovers six absolute vectors in 24 fresh worlds, compared with zero for each other policy on those same worlds. It retains correct ratios in all 24. Its final range is narrower in 15 worlds and tied in nine compared with information/rank. On those same fresh worlds, mean width relative to true scale is `47/192` for information/rank and `1765/10368` for overlap; median widths are `1/6` and `1/12`. Eighteen overlap-policy worlds retain intervals. [Fresh refinement analysis](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-acquisition/precision-analysis/analysis.json).
### 3.3 The check must measure the unresolved quantity

Under insufficient count uncertainty, information/rank produces a wrong unique absolute vector in 21 of 24 worlds. In world 2026103200 it infers `(6,3,8,1,2,4)` while the true values are `(12,6,16,2,4,8)`. All ten withheld whole–part relations have zero residual. Two withheld counts have residuals minus two and minus eight. Conservation checks preserve a common rescaling; independent counts address that remaining degree of freedom. [Saved case](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-acquisition/main/undercovered_counts-2026103200-information_rank.json).

This result guides verification design. A proposal inferred from ratios needs a scale-sensitive target. A proposal inferred from one measured count needs an independent count whose uncertainty is justified. The observation's mathematical relation to the remaining alternatives determines its ability to reject them.
### 3.4 Coordinate correspondence in a known account relation

The published khipu alignment matches 16 of 20 columns, with total absolute error 16. The lower records sum to 3,498 and the upper row to 3,482. Ordered flattening with known start and width preserves the prediction exactly. The reference alignment is the unique minimum-error result among 400 relative cyclic shifts. The best of 10,000 within-row shuffles has error 738; the best of 10,000 bag allocations has error 828. [Source aggregates](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/source-aggregate.json).

The scalar total difference remains 16 under every allocation, so it cannot distinguish the controls. The column-wise comparison measures the correspondence that the source's physical/account partition supplies.
### 3.5 Relation diversity in positional values

At eight complete accounts, 299 of 300 worlds identify the correct positional values. The remaining world has seven nonzero equations proportional to `−10u−9t+h=0` and one zero equation. The count fixes `u=1`. Both `(1,2,28)` and `(1,10,100)` satisfy the observed accounts. Repeating that carry relation leaves the free value unresolved.

Sibling permutations preserve every prefix. Removing membership leaves all 300 worlds ambiguous. Collapsing positions or scrambling membership rejects all 300 complete worlds by the eighth relation. Under full assumed membership, 97 incomplete worlds and 47 ownership worlds produce an incorrect unique decoder at some earlier prefix, then fail later. [KHI-01 numerical report](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/REPORT.md).
### 3.6 Consensus with uncertain associations

With two swapped assignments, the 75% consensus rule gives 281 correct, four wrong and fifteen ambiguous outcomes in 300 worlds; requiring every equation gives one correct outcome and 299 rejections. With four swaps, the 50% gate gives 200 correct, sixteen wrong and 84 ambiguous outcomes. The 75% gate rejects 297 worlds and accepts one correct, one wrong and one ambiguous set. Each final accepted wrong vector fails the independent checks. In one two-swap world, five true accounts repeat `-10u -9t +h = 0`; two corrupted accounts select `(1,11/2,119/2)` with seven votes, while the true vector has six. The saved exact geometry explains how a majority of individually correct relations can still identify a wrong point when their independent rank is low. [Frozen consensus report](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/robust-decoder/REPORT.md).
### 3.7 An independently recorded complete pool

In the fresh 200-seed collective experiment, two swapped assignments give 189 correct, two wrong and nine ambiguous outcomes under local consensus. Enforcing the complete-pool equality gives 197 correct, zero wrong and three ambiguous outcomes. For four swaps under the 50% gate, the corresponding counts are 133/9/58 and 190/1/9. With two missing local associations but a complete global inventory, correct recovery rises from 188 to 198. A declared partial pool gives 189 correct outcomes; treating that partial pool as complete gives fifteen accepted wrong points under the 50% gate and rejects every world under the 75% gate. [Collective results](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/conservation-check/REPORT.md).

At the final prefix, the correct complete-pool equation is the sum of the eight local equations. Its value comes from the independently recorded validity of the pooled relation when particular local associations are unreliable. Maximum consensus may discard some local equations while the collective relation remains binding. All comparisons reuse the same seed's quantities and have 200 independent base seeds.

One wrong baseline vector `(1,4/3,22)` passes all eight fresh account relations in world `20261020124-four_swapped`. Those equations have rank one and repeat the same carry relation. Three held-out count-feature rows have rank three and reject the vector, even if its scale is allowed to vary. In the counted view, a unit count of six gives `(6,8,132)` and count residuals `-4056`, `-1716` and `-3484`. The complete collective equation also rejects this point. This example makes the remaining validation requirement explicit: acquire measurements that separate the surviving values and scale. [Exact selected-case arithmetic](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/conservation-check/selected-case-arithmetic.json).
### 3.8 Validation choice and the remaining scale

The four-swap local-consensus population has nine wrong final rays. Three account-first checks leave one compatible. Greedy rank rejects all nine with two checks when the unit value has already been counted, or three without that anchor. Count-first needs fewer: one anchored count rejects all nine, while two unanchored counts do so. One unanchored count leaves all nine compatible because each wrong ray can adopt a different scale. The exact uniform-random expected counts remaining after three checks are .606 with the anchor and 2.024 without it. [Validation report and exact fractions](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/validation-design/REPORT.md).

Validation also filters tied optimum sets. Counted-view count-first with one check or greedy rank with two produces 190 correct absolute points and ten rejections from the original local-consensus sets. From the collective sets, either policy produces 199 correct points and rejects one. Unanchored count-first with two checks or greedy rank with three gives the same 199 collective recoveries. These are fixed-population post-outcome comparisons.

In the rank-one example, the first unanchored count selects the wrong absolute vector `(645/23,860/23,14190/23)` on the previously accepted ray. It fits `6v +8w = 5160`, as does the true vector `(6,60,600)`. A second count, `6u +6v +3w = 2196`, gives the wrong vector a residual of `1092/23` and rejects it. The saved intermediate point explains why scale identification alone can leave wrong ratios. Coefficient rank describes the selected rows; the original candidate constraints determine how many further measurements are needed.
## 4. Implications for collecting unfamiliar numerical records

The required observation table follows from these results. Each proposed relation needs a physical parent, its actual associated members, completeness, source coordinates, mark features and the basis for treating the relation as additive. A numerical reading also needs a measurement tied to an identified object and its units. An unresolved positive family shows which additional observation could distinguish the surviving values.
| Field to acquire | Record | Constraint it supplies |
| Physical identity | Registration, accession, source edition and exact figure/page | Joins observations to the same object and preserves aliases |
| Grouping and orientation | Parent, associated members, face adjacency, physical end and positional address | Defines which features participate in each relation |
| Completeness | Missing member, damaged area, recovery basis and surviving extent | Determines whether an equality, inequality or censored observation is appropriate |
| Graphic features | Counts, height/tier, form alternatives and image coordinates | Supplies coefficients and retains ambiguous alternatives |
| Quantity relation | Observed operation, its units and source basis | Gives the equation independently of assigned symbol values |
| Independent measurement | Named measured object, method, units and uncertainty | Fixes scale or separates remaining value assignments |
| Provenance | Original witness, copied descriptions and shared reconstruction | Identifies dependent observations and measurement errors |
| Reserved check | A separately acquired relation or scale-sensitive count | Tests the inferred values against information withheld during fitting |

The official Louvre record for Susa envelope SB 1940 describes three round pastilles and three rods inside, and three circular and three elongated exterior marks. That balanced mixture supplies one class-count row. It admits both a direct and a swapped two-class assignment in the project's design calculation. Unequal mixtures or individually associated imprint geometry would add distinguishing information. [Official accession](https://collections.louvre.fr/ark:/53355/cl010175973), [source-linked design calculation](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/physical-acquisition/susa-design-calculation.json). The accession and its documented contents provide a specific object for collecting those additional measurements.

For Indus objects, the current Harappa frame restores registrations and excavation keys for 22 incised tablets, and the Lothal audit links seal impressions with contact textures and support forms. Those records supply object provenance and operation hypotheses. A next numerical test needs an independently observed whole–part or measured-quantity relation attached to such an identified object. Acquisition should preserve original images and physical orientation before coding its features. [Harappa frame](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/harappa-object-frame/README.md), [Lothal frame](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/lothal-physical-use/README.md).
## 5. Verification, scope and availability

The simulations assume positive commensurate values, stable features and additive relations. Missingness is supplied when inequalities are used. The acquisition policy sees public costs and uncertainty descriptors. Base collections or base seeds are the independent units; prefixes, representations, policies and reused condition views share them. Point estimates describe these bounded designs. Mixed commodities, uncertain graphic identity and nonadditive functions require new models and controls.

PHYS-01 was checked by exact enumeration, rank over two prime fields and residual tests across 840 records. PHYS-02 arithmetic review checked 3,801 main states and 35,312 distinct saved certificates; the refinement review checked 993 states and 9,766 certificates. KHI-01 independent scalar sums checked 20,411 source predictions. Exact Gram determinants, row-space and witness checks covered all 36,000 simulation states, with 512 states independently checked by linear programming. The largest uncertainty in application is the observed relation and measurement model, which these arithmetic checks hold fixed.

KHI-03 checks all 12,000 prefixes and 384,768 exact subset states, retaining candidate and positivity witnesses. KHI-04 checks 11,200 prefixes, 716,820 subset states and 238,623 held-out residuals. A repaired static checker preserves its initial false flag beside unchanged fitting and scoring hashes. KHI-05 checks 33,600 deterministic validation records and independently classifies 59,856 random-subset intersections of ambiguous optimum sets. [Consensus verification](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/robust-decoder/main-v1/verification.json), [collective verification](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/conservation-check/verification-v2/verification.json), [validation reviews](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/validation-design/additional-review/verification.json).

Code, protocols, summaries, generated worlds, certificates and retrospectives are in the private project repository. Acquired database, source pages, manuscript and detailed source-derived vectors remain local with acquisition manifests and hashes. Frozen endpoints and post-outcome refinements have separate directories. [Claim-evidence map](claim-evidence-map.md), [reproduction and source package](methods.md).
# Methods package
The manuscript combines physical acquisition and known-system controls. Each branch retains its own design, answer keys and source exposure.

PHYS-01's corrected measurement endpoint supersedes its ownership-count diagnostics; original equations, ranks and old output remain preserved. PHYS-02's interval rule is an explicitly post-outcome refinement tested on fresh worlds. KHI-01 records prior exposure to the published target values and isolates predictor inputs computationally. Its generated answer keys are separate from the source replication.

Reproduction instructions and dependencies are in the branch READMEs and [KHI-01 RUNS](../../experiments/2026-10-02-six-hour/khipu-control/RUNS.md). Every completed run requires a fresh output directory. The local Python used for most calculations is 3.13, with NumPy and SciPy; endpoint manifests record actual versions. Exact arithmetic certificates form part of the output.

The source package retains original access routes, local paths, source hashes, field coverage and rights observations. Raw acquired khipu data and detailed source vectors are excluded from Git. The [redistribution record](../../knowledge/provenance/REDISTRIBUTION.md) governs future packaging. The generated controls and our own observations/code are the tracked reproducible part.

Before submission, supply authorship and affiliations, select a venue, resolve source-package access and data-use requirements, and obtain independent review of the archaeological observation design. The computational paper can be reviewed from its declared controls; an Indus value claim would require an eligible physical relation and separate measurement target.
